data.reasoning: The package is a standard Rust PAM module that downloads a pinned crate from crates.io and builds it using standard cargo commands. There is no top-level execution, no suspicious network activity, and no obfuscation. The 'inconclusive' verdict from the qwen model was caused by transient API errors (HTTP 400) rather than any security concerns. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and correctly determined the package is safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from a tool failure, not a security dispute. The qwen model encountered HTTP 400 errors when auditing the PKGBUILD and .nvchecker.toml, forcing an inconclusive result. The deepseek model successfully audited the same files and found them to be standard and safe.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review PKGBUILD and .nvchecker.toml due to API errors (HTTP 400)
learnings: Transient API errors should not force an overall 'inconclusive' verdict if other models successfully audit the critical files and find them safe.
The audit tool should clearly separate tool failures (like API timeouts or 400 errors) from actual security inconclusiveness to prevent unnecessary escalation triggers.
